paragraphs: Overall credibility is reported as unknown, for the static step s1 and for the overall conclusion. The results below are therefore for reference only and should not be read as converged or reliable.

In step s1, the reaction balance check passed: the applied load is balanced by the support reactions. The maximum von Mises stress, excluding the constrained faces, is {{s1.vm_max_mpa}}, and the maximum displacement is {{s1.u_max_mm}}. The material yield strength used is {{s1.strength_mpa}}.

The mesh quality check is unknown. Second-order elements on curved surfaces became too distorted after being upgraded, so straight-edged second-order elements were used and the curved surfaces are approximated by chords. Stress near curved surfaces may therefore deviate noticeably.

The mesh convergence checks for maximum stress and maximum displacement are reported as passed. Maximum stress across the successive mesh levels is {{s1.conv2.level0}}, {{s1.conv2.level1}} and {{s1.conv2.level2}}. Maximum displacement is {{s1.conv3.level0}}, {{s1.conv3.level1}} and {{s1.conv3.level2}}. These passes do not override the unknown mesh quality result, so overall credibility stays unknown.
No safety factor is given, because the credibility checks did not pass (the conclusion is unknown).

In the modal step m1, the lowest natural frequencies are {{m1.f1_hz}} ({{m1.f1_rpm}}), {{m1.f2_hz}} ({{m1.f2_rpm}}), {{m1.f3_hz}} ({{m1.f3_rpm}}) and {{m1.f4_hz}} ({{m1.f4_rpm}}). Only the part's own mass and stiffness are included, and the supports are ideal constraints. Real bearing stiffness would give lower frequencies, and any attached mass is not accounted for.

Limitations: the model is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions and were excluded from the maximum. Stress at sharp corners increases with mesh refinement (a theoretical singularity) and should not be used directly as a design basis.
suggestions: Refine the mesh on the curved surfaces so that several element layers span the curvature, then rerun the mesh quality check.
Re-run the analysis with a mesh in which second-order elements can be upgraded on curved surfaces without excessive distortion, to avoid the chord approximation.
Have an engineer review the stress near curved surfaces manually until the mesh quality check is resolved.
Have an engineer check the sharp corners in the model and consider adding a realistic fillet radius rather than relying on the singular corner stress.
Supply the bearing stiffness and the attached mass data so the modal frequencies can be recalculated under more realistic conditions.
Provide the required credibility inputs so that a safety factor can be evaluated once the checks pass.
